name: dotnet-channels

Guide to high-performance, thread-safe producer/consumer queues using `System.Threading.Channels`: bounded/unbounded creation, backpressure, `IAsyncEnumerable<T>`, graceful shutdown, and hosted services. See [skill:dotnet-background-services] and [skill:dotnet-csharp-async-patterns].

`Channel<T>` separates `ChannelWriter<T>` and `ChannelReader<T>`; multiple producers may call `WriteAsync`/`TryWrite` concurrently without external locking. Each item is read by exactly one consumer.

- Bounded: `Channel.CreateBounded<T>(capacity)` caps memory; preferred for production. `FullMode`: `Wait` (default; back-pressure), `DropOldest` (telemetry), `DropNewest`, or `DropWrite` (`TryWrite` returns `false`). Unbounded: `Channel.CreateUnbounded<T>()`; grows without limit and can exhaust memory under load. Unbounded -- use only when you control the producer rate.
- .NET 7+ bounded drop modes support an `itemDropped` callback for metrics, logging, rerouting, or cleanup (e.g. `(item as IDisposable)?.Dispose()`).
- Use `WriteAsync(item, cancellationToken)` for back-pressure; `TryWrite(item)` for non-blocking writes.
- Call `Complete()` or `TryComplete()` when no more items will be produced; `TryComplete()` is idempotent. `TryComplete(exception)` propagates errors to readers.
- Preferred drain loop:
  `while (await reader.WaitToReadAsync(ct)) while (reader.TryRead(out var item)) await ProcessAsync(item, ct);`
  This drains available items before awaiting. Alternatively use `ReadAsync(ct)`.
- Scale consumers with multiple tasks; use `BackgroundService` and `Task.WhenAll`. Create a DI scope per item when needed; handle processing exceptions and propagate cancellation.
- `ReadAllAsync(ct)` returns `IAsyncEnumerable<T>`; `await foreach` completes after closure and drain. Minimal APIs can return it to stream JSON. With NuGet package `System.Linq.Async`, compose async LINQ operators such as `.Where()` and `.Buffer()`.
- Bridge callback/producer feeds with a channel; complete the writer on success and `TryComplete(ex)` on failure.
- `SingleReader = true` /
